thread:
tomas: Quick heads-up — I pushed a prototype called FlashBridge that wraps FlashAttention v2/v3 and a small kernel selector. Need perf validation + rollout plan. TL;DR: dynamic selection by seq_len, kv_paging flag, and quant profile.

rachel: FlashBridge = new name for the integration shim? where's the code?

tomas: yes. it's a thin adapter so runtime can ask for 'flashbridge' and we pick v2/v3/fallback fused-attn. repo: git.redwood/inference/flashbridge. small config in canary: 
```
feature_flags:
  attn.flashbridge: on
kernel_selector:
  - name: flash_v3
    when: seq_len <= 1024 and quant != int8
  - name: flash_v2
    when: seq_len <= 2048
  - name: fused_attn
    when: default
kv_policy:
  paged_mode: prefer_paged_if_model_supports
  warmup_prefix_tokens: 64
```

kevin: benchmark numbers? any regressions vs current fused kernel?

tomas: microbench on a8g (single request, seq512, bs1): fused 10.4ms, flash_v2 8.9ms, flash_v3 6.7ms. throughput test (bs8, seq1024): fused 86 tok/s, flash_v2 110 tok/s, flash_v3 135 tok/s. caveat: when we hit paged-KV boundary (models with >1M params paged into multi-chunk KV), we saw +30–50% latency on v3 in the unoptimized path.

sara: that's the important part — kv paged behavior. do we have telemetry to detect paged hits?

kevin: yes, I added a label `kv_paged_hit` in perf events. we should also emit `kernel.chosen` and `kernel.fallback_reason`. quick query: 
```
select count(*) from perf_events where kernel.chosen = 'flash_v3' and kv_paged_hit = true;
```

rachel: rollout strategy? canary metrics?

tomas: propose phased rollout:
 1) internal canary: 5 hosts in staging, traffic routed 100% for a small model (gpt-mini) — 24h perf + mem checks
 2) prod canary: 1% traffic on non-critical model shard, feature flag attn.flashbridge=on for selected customers
 3) expand to 10% with autoscaling monitoring, enable adaptive batching heuristics per model
 4) full switch with automatic fallback to fused_attn if we observe >5% error or >20% p95 latency regressions for 1h

infra-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary rollout to cluster: staging-a @ 2026-03-18T09:30Z :rocket:

kevin: operational concerns: KV warmup — we should prefill the KV cache for commonly used prefixes (see config warmup_prefix_tokens). also need a short-circuit in selector: if model.kv_pages > 1 and kernel == flash_v3 then prefer fused_attn unless we've seen >80% paged hit ratio for that model.

sara: +1. also add perf guardrails in Console: expose per-model token/sec, p50/p95, kv_paged_hit rate, and kernel. add regression alert: psuedo-alert if token/sec drops >15% for 30m.

tomas: I'll open a short RFC with the selector logic and telemetry queries, add owners for the canary run. Owners: tomas (integration), kevin (telemetry & guards), rachel (canary ops), sara (KV behavior verification).

rachel: sounds good. can we include a tiny script to force fallback for testing?

tomas: yep, quick command: `curl -XPOST /admin/featureflag -d '{"flag":"attn.flashbridge","on":false,"reason":"test-fallback"}'` or use per-route override header `x-attn-kernel: fused_attn`.

kevin: one more thing — collect a small set of eval prompts that exercise long context + streaming so we catch subtle KV regressions. I'll add to /evals/flashbridge_long_context.json

infra-bot: note: monitoring policy created: infra/alerting/flashbridge-canary.yaml

rachel: OK let's run the staging canary tomorrow 09:30Z. tagging owners. :thumbsup:

sara: I'll run KV page profiler during canary and post a short summary in this thread.

kevin: if we see any regression we roll back flag to fused_attn for that model and file an incident. keep replies here for quick sync.

tomas: thanks all — will push RFC and invite reviewers.
